messages:
Alex: Hey team — we need to make a call on routing behavior for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers with egress restrictions. If the preferred model is not available locally, do we: 1) pick a compatible local variant, 2) route to a regional private replica, or 3) return an error? Thoughts?
Priya: My gut — prioritize locality and policy. Order: local variant > regional private cluster (same org/region) > deny. No public-hosted egress unless customer opts in.
Marc: +1. We also need to record *why* something was denied/redirected so Console + telemetry can explain the decision. Minimal audit fields: route_decision, reason_code, fallback_variant.
Lina: Agreed. From infra view, regional private fallback requires ensuring network peering & allowed regions. If peering missing, it should skip to deny.
Jamie: For product/UX: Console should show a small banner on the rollout page: "Requests are being served by fallback variant X due to egress policy" and a link to the routing audit event.
SecurityBot: Important: disallowed egress must be enforced in control plane so we never leak data to public endpoints. Also add a policy-level flag: "allow_hosted_fallback": false by default for Private customers.
Marc: Implementation note: internal routing API needs an explicit hint field: `egress_preference: ["local","regional","hosted"]` and a resolved `final_route` in the response. That avoids ad-hoc logic in callers.
Alex: What about billing/quotas? If we route to a regional private replica, do we bill as Hosted or Dedicated? Need consistent semantics.
Priya: Bill as Dedicated/Private — it's still within customer-dedicated capacity. Only hosted endpoints increment hosted costs. Put this in the policy doc.
Lina: Ops: we should add a circuit-breaker that flips to "deny" if inter-region latency or failures exceed threshold for X minutes. Otherwise a slow fallback will degrade apps.
Jamie: UX: Add a toggle per-customer "Allow regional fallback" with tooltip: "If turned on, requests may route to other private clusters in allowed regions when local capacity is exceeded." Default off.
Marc: For telemetry/backtraces, add `routing.reason` tags to traces and a compact event in request logs like: `routing_event:{decision:local_variant,rule:egress_policy_v1}`. This helps SLOs and regression alerts.
Alex: Small policy sample for the control plane (draft):
```json
{
  "policy_id": "vpc-routing-2026-03",
  "allow_hosted_fallback": false,
  "allow_regional_fallback": true,
  "allowed_regions": ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"],
  "fallback_order": ["local_variant","regional_cluster","deny"],
  "audit_fields": ["route_decision","reason_code","resolved_variant"]
}
```
Priya: Nice. We also need an explicit deny code that surfaces to customers: `DENY_NO_ROUTE_EGRESS` so support can quickly filter.
SecurityBot: Add KMS context and ensure audit logs include `customer_id` and `request_id` but strip any model outputs.
ops-bot: FYI — I'll add a gating check in the deploy pipeline that prevents enabling `allow_hosted_fallback` for any Private environment until Security approves.
Jamie: Can we ship a canary where the control plane emits the routing decision but still follows old behavior? We can turn on observability-only first.
Marc: Yes — implement a `routing.log_only=true` mode. After 2 weeks of no anomalies, flip to enforced.
Alex: Action items: 1) Marc — PR for routing API change (egress_preference + resolved_route) 2) Lina — run a checklist for cross-region peering constraints 3) Priya/Jamie — Console knob + banner copy 4) SecurityBot — policy for hosted fallback opt-in 5) ops-bot — deploy gate. Assign and rough ETA?
Marc: I'll have the API PR by EOD Friday (1782460000).
Lina: Peering checklist in a doc by Monday.
Priya: UX mock + copy by Tuesday.
SecurityBot: I'll draft the approval rubric and required audit fields by end of week.
Alex: Thanks all — sounds like consensus. We'll start with observability-only canary and iterate. :thumbsup:
